skill.name: socialdatax-media-save-organizer
skill.description: Save images, videos, and audio from supported social platforms using SocialDataX commands, with source links, local paths, and individual download results.
skill.summary: Organize requested social media downloads into separate local folders with verified results and a source manifest.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: All 38 static alerts are false positives for their reported patterns: Markdown backticks, documented credential names, provider links, and readable Chinese text. Separate semantic risks involve executing an unpinned npm package and requiring token-bearing XHS URLs in shared outputs without redaction. No evidence found of credential harvesting, encoded payloads, or instructions to override this audit.

remediation.issue: Commands execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx with automatic confirmation, outside the reviewed package contents.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and verify its provenance and integrity before execution. Obtain approval before installing or running downloaded dependencies.

remediation.issue: XHS output instructions forbid redacting xsec_token parameters, including when forwarding or publishing source URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep complete URLs only in private, authorized manifests. Redact token parameters from shared outputs by default and obtain consent before including complete links.

content.user_title: Save and Organize Social Media Files
content.value_statement: Social media files often lack a clear record of their sources and download status. This skill guides SocialDataX downloads and organizes verified files with source manifests.
actual_capabilities: Resolve supplied content links through SocialDataX commands for Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X, and Bilibili.
Save available images, videos, or audio from direct media URLs using platform-specific download commands.
Place distinct media items in separate subdirectories within the user-selected output directory.
Deduplicate repeated media URLs while retaining their associated sources.
Record platforms, source links, local paths, media types, download results, and failure reasons.
Verify actual files and distinguish new downloads from existing files or failed requests.
limitations: This package provides instructions, not the downloader implementation; execution depends on the external SocialDataX CLI.
Requires Node.js and npm for CLI execution, ffmpeg for Bilibili merging, and an API key for online detail or download-link requests.
Supports only the documented platforms and available media; it cannot guarantee successful downloads or invent missing media links.
Current instructions use an unpinned npm package and require complete token-bearing XHS URLs; review dependency trust and sharing permissions before use.

use_cases.title: Collect Approved Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Save selected campaign media from supplied links and provide source-to-file records with individual success and failure results.

use_cases.title: Maintain Research Source Records
use_cases.description: Organize a defined set of social media sources into separate folders and track missing or unavailable media.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Editing Materials
use_cases.description: Collect requested images, clips, or audio without automatically downloading unwanted covers or background music.

prompt_templates.title: Save One Media File
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this direct media URL: [media URL]. Use [output directory] and report the verified local path or the actual failure reason.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: download one known media file.

prompt_templates.title: Collect Files From One Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Save the images from [supported post URL] into [output directory]. List each source, local path, and result without downloading unrelated media.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: resolve a post before downloading selected media.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a Mixed Platform Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Process only these links: [link list]. Save requested media under [output directory], using separate subdirectories. Deduplicate media URLs and report failures without inventing paths.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: manage a defined batch across supported platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Resume a Verified Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue [link list] using [existing manifest] and [output directory]. Verify existing files against their sources. Retry unresolved items and keep shared output free of token-bearing URLs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reconcile existing files and apply explicit sharing restrictions.

output_examples.input: Save images from two supplied posts and report the results.
output: Illustrative result: two images saved from the first post in its separate output subdirectory.
Second post: no image URL returned; no file saved.
The private source manifest lists each source, verified local path, media type, and result.

output_examples.input: Resume a collection using its existing source manifest.
output: Illustrative result: one existing file verified against its recorded source; no new download counted.
One missing video downloaded into a separate empty subdirectory.
One unavailable item retained as a failure with its actual error.

best_practices: Provide an explicit link list, requested media types, and output directory; review and approve a pinned CLI dependency before execution.
Verify actual files against command results and maintain source mappings before treating existing files as completed downloads.
Keep token-bearing source URLs in private records and explicitly prohibit their inclusion in shared reports.
anti_patterns: Do not supply content pages where direct media URLs are required or guess missing download addresses.
Do not treat command submission or skipped_existing as proof that a new file was saved.
Do not run unreviewed dependency updates or publish complete token-bearing links without authorization.

faq.question: Which platforms are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X or Twitter, and Bilibili.

faq.question: Does every download require an API key?
faq.answer: No. Direct media downloads do not require one; online content details and Bilibili download-link requests use SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY.

faq.question: Which local dependencies are required?
faq.answer: CLI execution requires Node.js and npm. Bilibili merging also requires ffmpeg.

faq.question: How are existing files handled?
faq.answer: Existing files count as verified only when their source mapping matches. Otherwise, the workflow uses a separate empty subdirectory instead of overwriting files.

faq.question: What happens when a download fails?
faq.answer: Successful files remain available. The report retains failed items and actual errors; insufficient balance stops repeated retries until the account issue is resolved.

faq.question: Are source manifests safe to share publicly?
faq.answer: Not by default. The skill requires complete XHS URLs containing xsec_token; keep original links private and redact token parameters before sharing.
